heading: REGENT OF EAST HALMAHERA
REGIONAL HOUSE OF REPRESENTATIVES
translated_text:
REGIONAL HOUSE OF REPRESENTATIVES

OF EAST HALMAHERA REGENCY

AND

REGENT OF EAST HALMAHERA REGENCY

DECIDES:

REGIONAL REGULATION OF EAST HALMAHERA REGENCY CONCERNING PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN.

heading: CHAPTER I
translated_text:
CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is the Region of East Halmahera Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regional Government of East Halmahera Regency.
3. Regent is the Regent of East Halmahera.
4. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and DPRD in the administration of Government Affairs which are the authority of the Region.
5. Technical Regional Apparatus is a Regional Apparatus whose scope of duties and responsibilities includes the affairs of Women's Empowerment and/or Child Protection.
6. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb.
7. Woman is a human being of female sex and a person who is recognized by law as a woman.
8. Women's Empowerment is every effort to improve physical, mental spiritual, social capacity, knowledge, and skills so that women are ready to be utilized according to their respective abilities.
9. Fulfillment of Children's Rights is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate, optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
10. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering either physically, sexually, psychologically, and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or deprivation of a person's freedom unlawfully.

11. Victim is a woman and/or child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.

12. Protection is all preventive, service and empowerment actions to protect and guarantee the rights of women and children from acts of violence.
13. Prevention is activities carried out to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children.
14. Service is action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is or has occurred.
15. Empowerment is the strengthening of women victims of violence to be able to work and work independently after they are recovered and provided with health and social rehabilitation services.
16. Health Rehabilitation is an effort to restore the condition of victims including physical, psychological and social health so that victims can carry out their roles again properly and reasonably both in the family and in society.

17. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly.

18. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of violence from the regional area to the area of origin.
19. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.
20. Integrated Service Center for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter abbreviated as P2PTP2A, is the Regional Technical Implementation Unit (UPTDD) of the Integrated Service Center for the Protection of Women and Children integrated into the technical Regional Apparatus of East Halmahera Regency.

Forms of Women's Empowerment

heading: Article 5
translated_text:
Article 5

1. In order to improve the position, role, and quality of women, as well as efforts to realize gender equality and justice in family life, society, nation, and state, women must be empowered.
2. Women's empowerment as referred to in paragraph (1) is directed to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings, so that they are able to play a role and participate in economic, socio-cultural, political, and legal activities.

Article 6 (1) The Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility in efforts to empower women.

2. Women's empowerment efforts as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out in an integrated manner in accordance with applicable laws and regulations.

heading: Article 7
Article 8
translated_text:
Article 8

Empowerment of women in the socio-cultural field as referred to in Article 5 paragraph (2) shall be implemented through: a enhancement of knowledge, attitudes and skills to encourage the fulfillment of tiered education in accordance with potential to improve social status;

b enhancement of awareness, willingness and ability to overcome health problems through quality promotive, preventive, curative, and rehabilitative efforts, primarily in the field of reproductive health.

c enhancement of awareness and knowledge about independent, healthy and prosperous family planning including access to consultation services and marriage registration; and d facilitation and efforts to preserve customs and the development of science, technology, arts and culture for the advancement of women.

heading: Article 9
Article 10
translated_text:
Article 10

(1) The implementation of women's empowerment in the legal field as referred to in Article 5 paragraph (2) includes:
a enhancement of awareness and knowledge in the legal field through communication, information and education services; and b facilitation of access and legal consultation services.

2. The implementation of women's empowerment in the legal field as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out in accordance with applicable laws and regulations.

heading: Article 11
Paragraph 3
translated_text:
Paragraph 3

Community Participation

heading: Article 12
translated_text:
Article 12

1. To carry out women's empowerment as referred to in Article 6, the Regional Government may involve community participation.
2. Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by individuals, Social Community Institutions, religious institutions and/or other legitimate institutions.

Rights and Obligations of Children

heading: Article 13
Article 14
Paragraph 2
translated_text:
Paragraph 2

Birth Registration

heading: Article 15
translated_text:
Article 15

The Implementation of Fulfillment of Children's Rights in the field of birth registration, as referred to in Article 13 letter a, the Regional Government is obliged to organize the registration of children's births with the issuance of birth certificates in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

heading: Paragraph 3
translated_text:
Paragraph 3

Health

heading: Article 16
translated_text:
Article 16

1. The Implementation of Fulfillment of Children's Rights in the field of health as referred to in Article 13 letter b, the Regional Government is obliged to provide facilities and organize comprehensive health services for children, so that every child obtains optimal health status from the womb which is carried out in stages adjusted to the regional financial capacity and supported by community participation.
2. Comprehensive health services as referred to in paragraph (1) include:a. promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative efforts for basic health services;
b. exemption from cost burdens for malnourished children, children undergoing dialysis due to kidney failure, children with thalassemia major, children with disabilities, children with special needs, street children, children infected with HIV/AIDS, child workers, children victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic and other addictive substances (NAPZA) abuse, children who are victims of violence, such as neglect, economically exploited, sexually exploited and victims of human trafficking.
3. Children as referred to in paragraph (2) are children from poor families except as otherwise regulated in accordance with the health financing program established by the government.

heading: Article 17
translated_text:
Article 17

The Regional Government, community, family and parents must endeavor to ensure that children born are protected from diseases that threaten the continuity of life and/or cause disability.

heading: Paragraph 4
translated_text:
Paragraph 4

Education

heading: Article 18
translated_text:
Article 18

(1) The Implementation of Fulfillment of Children's Rights in the field of education as referred to in Article 13 letter c, the Regional Government shall guarantee the implementation of a 12 (twelve) year compulsory education program for all children.

2. Every organizer of an education unit is obliged to provide opportunities for children to obtain educational services without discrimination.

heading: Article 19
translated_text:
Article 19

Every organizer of an education unit is prohibited from expelling children from educational institutions unless there is a guarantee for the continuity of the child's education.

heading: Article 20
translated_text:
Article 20

Every organizer of an education unit is obliged to coordinate with relevant child protection agencies if they find children dropping out of school due to being victims of acts of violence.

heading: Article 21
translated_text:
Article 21

Children with disabilities and children with special needs are given equal opportunities to obtain formal, non-formal and informal education services, including special and inclusive education.

heading: Article 22
translated_text:
Article 22

Early Childhood Education for children aged 0 (zero) to 3 (three) years and 4 (four) to 6 (six) years may be organized by Posyandu institutions, Taman Posyandu, Early Childhood Education Posts and similar Early Childhood Education unit institutions.

heading: Article 24
Article 25
Article 26
Part Three
translated_text:
Part Three

Forms of Violence

heading: Article 27
Article 28
translated_text:
Article 28

Physical violence as referred to in Article 27 letter a is caused by acts that result in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death.

heading: Article 29
translated_text:
Article 29

Psychological violence as referred to in Article 27 letter b is caused by acts that result in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/ or severe psychological suffering to a person.

heading: Article 30
Article 31
Article 32
translated_text:
Article 32

Exploitation as referred to in Article 27 letter e is caused by:
a. acts that exploit economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others;
b. acts with or without the victim's consent including prostitution, forced labor or service, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/ or body tissues or exploiting the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain material or immaterial benefits; and/ or c. all forms of exploitation of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all prostitution or indecency activities.

heading: Article 33
translated_text:
Article 33

Other violence as referred to in Article 27 letter f is caused by:
a. threats of violence comprising: any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without using means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom; and b. coercion, comprising: a situation where a person/victim is ordered to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will.

Article 35

Part Five

Handling of Women and Children Victims of Violence

heading: Article 36
Article 37
Article 38
translated_text:
Article 38

Complaint, consultation, and counseling services as referred to in Article 37 letter a include:
a. initial identification or recording of victims;
b. case identification; andc. determination of actions to be taken.

heading: Article 39
Article 40
translated_text:
Article 40

Medical rehabilitation services as referred to in Article 37 letter c include:
a. first aid to victims;
b. treatment and recovery of physical injuries aimed at restoring the physical condition of victims carried out by medical personnel and paramedics; andc. referral to health services.

heading: Article 41
translated_text:
Article 41

1. Social rehabilitation services as referred to in Article 37 letter d constitute services provided in order to restore the traumatic condition of victims.
2. Forms of services as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be through social support.
3. Social support as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be carried out through:a. spiritual guidance to victims; andb. psychological recovery of victims.

heading: Article 42
Article 43
translated_text:
Article 43

1. Social reintegration services as referred to in Article 37 letter f aim to return victims to their families and social environment.
2. Social reintegration services as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by the Regional Government in coordination with:  a. related agencies and institutions both government and non-government; andb. village community institutions and/or local community leaders.

heading: CHAPTER IV
translated_text:
CHAPTER IV

INTEGRATED SERVICE CENTER FOR THE PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN (P2TP2A)

heading: Article 44
CHAPTER V
Article 46
CHAPTER VI
Article 49
translated_text:
Article 49

1. Every operator of internet service businesses, play stations and types of children's games based on information and communication technology is required to manage and design child-friendly places.
2. Every business operator as referred to in paragraph (1) shall: a regulate rooms/booths with adequate lighting and not closed;  b not accept children wearing uniforms and/or during school hours;

c locally block sites containing elements of pornography and pornographic acts; and d limit visiting hours and supervise the use of available facilities.

heading: CHAPTER VII
translated_text:
CHAPTER VII

MONITORING AND EVALUATION

Article 50

1. To ensure synergy, balance and effectiveness of integrated measures in the implementation of policies, programs, activities, protection of Women and children, the Government conducts monitoring.
2. Monitoring as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out by technical Regional Apparatus and P2TP2A.
3. Monitoring as referred to in paragraph (1) is to determine the progress and obstacles in the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the Protection of Women and children.
4. Monitoring is carried out periodically through coordination and direct monitoring of Regional Apparatus implementing policies, activities for the protection of Women and child victims of violence.

heading: Article 51
translated_text:
Article 51

1. Evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the Protection of Women and child victims of violence is carried out at the end of each Budget year or if necessary according to needs.
2. The results of the evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the protection of Women and child victims of violence are used as input for the formulation of policies, programs and activities for the protection of Women and child victims of violence for the following year.
3. Evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

heading: CHAPTER VIII
translated_text:
CHAPTER VIII

FINANCING

Article 52

Funding for the implementation of Protection of Women and children, is sourced from:
a. Regional revenue and expenditure budget; and/orb. Other legitimate and non-binding sources in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

heading: CHAPTER IX
translated_text:
CHAPTER IX

GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Article 53

1. The Regent conducts guidance and supervision over the implementation of this regional regulation.
2. Guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) includes providing implementation instructions, guidance, supervision, monitoring and evaluation of the Implementation of Protection of Women and Children.

heading: CHAPTER X
translated_text:
CHAPTER X

COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION

Article 54

1. In the implementation of Protection of Women and children, the community may:a. form family partners at the Village/Sub-district level by the community;
b. conduct socialization of women's and children's rights independently;
c. provide first aid to victims; andd. report to the competent authority if violence against victims occurs in their environment.
2. Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out by individuals, community institutions, non-governmental organizations, educational institutions, religious institutions, private sector and/or mass media.

heading: CHAPTER XI
translated_text:
CHAPTER XI

ADMINISTRATIVE SANCTIONS

Article 55

1. Any person or business entity that violates the provisions as referred to in Article 47, Article 48, Article 49 shall be subject to administrative sanctions in the form of: a Written warning;

b Suspension of license;

c Administrative fine; and d Revocation of license.

2. Written warning as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a is given 3 (three) times with a grace period between one warning and another of at least 1 (one) month.
3. Suspension of License as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b is imposed if a written warning has been given as referred to in paragraph (2).
4. Suspension of License as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b may be withdrawn if the person or business entity committing the violation pays an administrative fine of Rp. 30,000,000,- (thirty million rupiah).
5. If within the period specified in the license suspension, the administrative fine is not paid, then the license will be revoked.

heading: CHAPTER XII
translated_text:
CHAPTER XII

CLOSING PROVISIONS

Article 56

At the latest 1 (one) year, calculated from the effective date of this Regional Regulation, the Implementing Regulations of this Regional Regulation must have been stipulated.

heading: Article 57
translated_text:
Article 57

This Regional Regulation comes into force on the date of promulgation.

So that everyone may know of it, orders the promulgation of this Regional Regulation by placing it in the Regional Gazette of East Halmahera Regency.

heading: ELUCIDATION
translated_text:
ELUCIDATION

OF

REGIONAL REGULATION OF EAST HALMAHERA REGENCY

NUMBER 7 YEAR 2022

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights so that their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and destiny without discrimination. In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in East Halmahera so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, protection needs to be provided to women and child victims of violence in the form of regional regulations. So far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and child victims of violence have not regulated protection measures in the Region so that institutional and regulatory support is needed to ensure its implementation. Regional Regulations regulate protection efforts for victims, especially in terms of prevention, services and empowerment of women and child victims of violence in East Halmahera.
